title: Skip rows with OFFSET
description: Write a query that returns the `name` and `price` of products 4 through 6 when sorted by price descending (skip the top 3, then take the next 3).
hints: OFFSET n skips the first n rows of the sorted result before LIMIT starts counting - the two combine for pagination: OFFSET 3 LIMIT 3 means 'skip 3, then take 3'.
Sort products by price descending, OFFSET 3, then LIMIT 3.
expected_behavior: Returns the 4th, 5th, and 6th most expensive products.
solution: SELECT name, price FROM products ORDER BY price DESC OFFSET 3 LIMIT 3;
explanation: OFFSET and LIMIT both act on the already-sorted result - OFFSET decides where to start counting, LIMIT decides how many rows to take from that point, which together is exactly how page 2 of a paginated list is built.
